title: Claude in Your Workflow
description: Integrate Claude into the tools you already use — Notion, Slack, automation platforms, and custom applications.

data.text: Understanding the Claude API is the first step. The next step is connecting Claude to the tools you actually use. This lesson covers common integration patterns: adding Claude to Slack for team assistance, connecting Claude to Notion for document automation, using no-code platforms to build Claude-powered workflows, and building custom integrations with webhooks.

data.title: Common ways to integrate Claude:
items: Slack bot — ask Claude questions directly in Slack channels
Notion integration — auto-generate and summarize Notion pages
Email assistant — draft and refine emails through a connected inbox
Custom app — build a web app with Claude as the intelligence layer
Automation platform — use Zapier, Make, or similar to trigger Claude actions

data.text: Adding Claude to Slack transforms it from a chat app into a team knowledge assistant. Team members can @mention the Claude bot to ask questions, summarize threads, draft messages, or analyze documents. The integration uses the Slack API to receive messages and the Claude API to generate responses.

data.title: Slack + Claude use cases
data.text: Common Slack-Claude integrations include: summarizing long threads when you join late, drafting announcements for the team, answering questions about internal documentation, and translating messages between team members who speak different languages.

Notion is a natural fit for Claude integration because it is a content-rich workspace. You can build a Claude-powered assistant that: auto-generates page content from templates, summarizes long database entries, extracts action items from meeting notes, and translates content between languages. The integration uses the Notion API to read and write pages.

You do not need to write code to integrate Claude. Platforms like Zapier, Make (formerly Integromat), and n8n let you connect Claude to hundreds of apps using visual workflows. For example: when a new Google Doc is created, send its content to Claude for summarization, then post the summary to Slack.

data.title: No-code workflow example
data.content: Zapier workflow: Trigger: New email in Gmail with label 'Newsletter'. Action 1: Extract email body. Action 2: Send to Claude API with prompt 'Summarize this newsletter in 3 bullet points'. Action 3: Post summary to a Slack channel. Result: You get curated newsletter summaries automatically.

data.text: For full control, build a custom application that calls the Claude API directly. This is the approach used by companies building AI-powered products. The basic architecture is simple: your frontend sends user input to your backend, your backend formats it into a Claude API request, and your backend returns Claude's response to the frontend.

data.title: Security best practices for integrations:
items: Never expose your API key in client-side code (browsers, mobile apps)
Use a backend proxy to make all Claude API calls
Implement rate limiting to prevent abuse
Log API usage for monitoring and cost tracking
Review Anthropic's data handling policies before processing sensitive data

data.title: Data privacy matters
data.text: When integrating Claude into workflows that handle sensitive data (customer PII, financial information, health data), review Anthropic's data processing agreement and business associate agreement. Do not send sensitive data to the API without understanding the data handling terms.

data.title: Integration takeaways
points: Slack and Notion are the most popular Claude integration targets
No-code platforms like Zapier let you integrate Claude without writing code
Custom apps use the API directly via a backend server
Always use a backend proxy — never expose API keys in client-side code
Review data handling policies before processing sensitive information
